extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, communications/marketing teams, and anyone writing or distributing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and formatting newswire press releases that attract media pickup and reach target audiences, covering structure, style, SEO, and distribution best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary attention-grabbing line that answers 'Why should I care?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 100 characters (structure); when possible stay under 70 characters (headline guidelines). Use strong action verbs, write in active voice implying immediate relevance, be clear and direct, include relevant keywords and numbers/data supporting the claim. Example note: 'unveil' and 'reveal' generate more engagement than 'launch'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: City and date of issuance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the city and the release date at the top of the release to establish timeliness and location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary using the five Ws (who, what, when, where, why)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the essential information so journalists can quickly grasp the story; this paragraph should succinctly answer the five Ws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body content
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting details with short paragraphs containing one idea each
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short paragraphs, each with a single idea; provide context, background, and relevant facts that support the lead without overwhelming readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement from a relevant stakeholder or expert for credibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one quote from a knowledgeable source to add authority and human perspective; introduce speakers with full name and title (per AP style).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics, survey results, or industry trends backing claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with data from reputable sources (statistics, research, industry reports) to build credibility and increase pickup chances; cite sources where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to action (CTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear next steps (website link, registration, contact info)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a single, explicit CTA aligned with the release's primary goal (e.g., link to register, visit a webpage, contact for interviews). Ensure the CTA is easy to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief organizational description highlighting mission
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a concise paragraph about the organization at the end of the release to give journalists context about the issuer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Names, emails, phone numbers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List full names, email addresses, and phone numbers for media inquiries so reporters can readily reach spokespeople or PR contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Images, video, or other engaging visual elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to high-quality visuals (images, video, assets) to increase engagement and utility for newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand readers—industry professionals or potential customers—and tailor messaging accordingly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target language, tone, and angle to what resonates with the intended audience to improve relevance and pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain clarity and focus; avoid unnecessary detail
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for 300 to 500 words for typical releases to cover essential information without overwhelming readers. Use tight prose where each word adds value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect the story to current trends or broader social issues that matter to the target audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the announcement within topical themes or industry trends to increase newsworthiness and the likelihood of media interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a story
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanize content by weaving a compelling narrative with beginning, middle, and end
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include perspectives from affected individuals or stakeholders to make the release more relatable and engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize press release for search engines and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use relevant keywords, optimize headlines and subheads, and include backlinks to improve search visibility and reach broader audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Back claims with reputable evidence to build trust
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite statistics, research, or industry reports from reputable sources; transparent sourcing increases trust and pickup chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include strong call to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct readers toward the next step aligned with the release's primary goal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the intended action explicit and easy (e.g., clear links, registration instructions, contact methods). The CTA should reinforce the release objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and refine
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread and edit thoroughly for grammar, style, and flow
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each word adds value; check accuracy, clarity, and AP-style compliance before distribution. Refinement improves professionalism and reduces errors that deter pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release length considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose length appropriate to the news importance and complexity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter releases (~300 words) work for minor updates, time-sensitive news, or event teasers. Longer releases suit complex topics requiring technical explanation, research presentations, or significant announcements (mergers, leadership changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: AP Style Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Key formatting and style conventions to follow (AP style)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP formatting rules: capitalize only the first word and proper nouns in headlines; spell out numbers one through nine and use numerals for 10+; write full month names when standalone and abbreviate when used with specific dates; use double quotation marks and introduce speakers with full name and title; capitalize job titles only before names; spell out acronyms on first use with abbreviation in parentheses; use one space after periods; avoid Oxford commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of numbers/data in headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Include numbers or data in headlines when relevant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers can increase headline engagement and clarity—use them where they strengthen the claim or quantify impact.
